summary.text: Bob Fioretti is the Republican nominee for Illinois Attorney General. A Chicago attorney trained in civil rights law and a two-term alderman of the 2nd Ward from 2007 to 2015, he has run unsuccessfully for mayor, Cook County state's attorney and Cook County Board president.

paragraphs.text: Fioretti was born in Chicago, where he still lives, and graduated from Mendel High School.
He earned a B.A. in political science from the University of Illinois and a J.D. from Northern Illinois University.
He trained as a civil rights attorney and worked as an attorney with the law firm Orum & Roth.
According to the Sun-Times, he has also worked as an assistant Illinois attorney general and has courtroom experience with the City Hall corporation counsel's office.
He oversaw the Historic Pullman Foundation and the Judicial Evaluation Committee of the Chicago Bar Association Executive Committee.
Fioretti served as alderman for Chicago's 2nd Ward from 2007 to 2015.
Since leaving the City Council he has run unsuccessfully twice for mayor, for Cook County state's attorney and for Cook County Board president.
He is challenging Democratic incumbent Kwame Raoul in the November 3, 2026 general election.
